item.title: SCP: Kingdom Come my first tale
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

page type tale

genre: horror

page layout a transcript of a conversation with passages from the book revelations used as a framing device

Elevator pitch: Going off of what was established in the tale "new job". A former researcher on his death bed shares visions of an apocalyptic battle between SCP-999 and the scarlet king.

central narrative: while being read his last rites, the dying man interrupts the priest and starts yelling about his visions. The priest tries to tell him to save his strength, but the man insists he must listen. The visions begin with a great war between the SCP foundation and 6 other groups of interests, the war being about weather to destroy anomalies, study them, or let them be. The War comes to a head with an all out seige on site 19, where SCP-988 is being kept. During the battle, SCP-999 supposedly dies to save a researcher from SCP-049. That researcher then finds and opens SCP-988 The visions then skip ahead to the end of the seige, where SCP-053 and 682 are united and release some of the most dangerous SCPs. The survivors of the ensuing chaos come together despite their differences to try and stop this army of SCPs, and the Scarlet king feeds off the chaos of this battle. Pretty soon a portal to the scarlet king's world rips open and fire rains down as the Scarlet king enters our world. Just then SCP-999 reappears with a handful of other thaumiel class SCPs. Unfortunately the man dies before he can tell the man how it ends, but he does leave him with a warning not to "face the light when the day comes" before passing away.

hook: its an end of the world prediction that sorta lines up with the book of revelations.

item.title: A (Real) Cognitohazard
item.content:encoded:
Hi,

I'm planning on writing a meta SCP article on the McCollough effect. Thing is, I suppose you could say this is a real-life cognitohazard. Viewing the images can alter the way your brain perceives colour, causing long-lasting changes to colour perception. In some cases, the effects have lasted months after initial viewing.

I could totally do this… there are McCollough images that are CC compliant. Thing is, this could affect people in real life. I guess I would need some sort of disclaimer warning the reader of the image, but people are just going to assume the warning is fictional. It's not, and these images can alter you in real life.

I don't know how to write a disclaimer that will properly inform the reader of the potential repercussions whilst not breaking the tone of the site.

item.title: Re: The innate nature of things.
item.content:encoded:
hewwo

Initial thoughts: I like the idea. Kind the boiler room or dev room of the universe. It's a neat idea and there's a lot of room to explore and for the Foundation to start to uncover the laws and mechanisms of magic.

more thoughts
less thoughts

I do, however, have some issues with the concept. The biggest thing that sticks out to me is security. While it would make sense that it would be guarded against people who would inadvertently mess with the wrong machine and destroy the universe, robots or something constantly being alert to murder anyone who enters feels very cliche and inelegant. As you said, this is not an easy place to reach. If I were the Architect of the Universe and left behind a room of glorious engines, I would expect the people who found it to be powerful sages or natural explorers rather than raiders. To me, it would feel more natural if the security was a guide who was peaceful, helpful, and explained things up until the point that an engine was destroyed or tampered with.

However, if you were to take an eldritch slant, you could make it so understand these machines is like a fish trying to understand its aquarium filter. Then deadly security forces would be understandable.

Beyond that, it feels like a very dry story. Like cybersqyd said, it's kind of a passive, foundation poking around kind of deal. Like they really can't touch the machines or it could collapse the sun so why are they there?

If you can give me a good answer as to what the story would be, I'll give you my greenlight.

item.title: Re: Black-Rock: my first SCP
item.content:encoded:
[+] open for crit
– hide block

central narrative: none at the moment but I'm open to ideas

This is a pretty big dealbreaker for me. A good SCP article to me is a short story about a weird thing and how the Foundation interacts with it

However, when a person with anomalous abilities touches it, their body will instead turn into a new crystal with glowing runes seemingly etched into it.

'anomalous' doesn't function as a like…proper physical category of thing. Treating all kinds of anomalies as being the same kinda…feels really iffy because like why would memetic/cognitohazards work the same as like, reality bending or like, conceptual anomalies or like a factory that makes teddy bears filled guts or w/e.

At the end of the day my big concern is 'crystal that grows more crystal in people' is somewhat cliche and also that you don't really do anything with it. It might be really worth thinking about questions like "what makes this interesting to read about?" and "what challenges does its existence pose for the foundation?" and like, really figure out what you can do here to explore this thing in a more interesting way.

item.content:encoded:

foundation discovers common abstract mechanism enabling magic. Through prodding it manage to open a door to ES.

Is this a 'mechanism' as in like, a physical machine? or a mechanism as in an abstract process?

Security is tight and progress becomes harder as they get further in.

What's the security like here? How does it make progress harder?

This feels…like a really weird way to solve this problem

Where did the machines come from and what would happen if they were switched off?

these are interesting questions for it to raise but it feels like there's nothing here really hinting at any kind of interesting answers to them?

My concern here overall is that the narrative here feels very passive: there's not a lot driving the Foundations investigation of this forward so it feels like it might be hard to keep a reader on board during the ride. It might be worth considering what the stakes/conflict are here: like, what happens if the foundation fails? What happens if the foundation succeeds? What forces are trying to prevent the foundation succeeding? Why do the foundation keep working against those forces?

It might be worth considering who is the 'face' of this investigation too: like, who are the characters that are in charge of driving the investigation forward and what are their motivations here?

item.title: Re: Radio Virus SCP seeking green light
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

Central narrative:

What I'm really looking for out of a central narrative section is 'what does the article contain': you've mostly used it to expand on what the SCP does; and I'm left wondering what the Foundation's role in all this is and like…what the actual article would look like.

Like bear in mind: you're trying to write a short story about a weird thing disguised as a technical report; not an encyclopedia entry on it; and so what you do with the SCP is a lot more important than just what the SCP can do.

each mind-swap creates a copy of the host of the radio show.

"mind-swap" implies "the listener and the host swap minds"; but it seems like you mean "the host overwrites the listener's mind" here?

Once they spread the virus, they turn into ruthless monsters.

Why do they turn into ruthless monsters? What does this look like? Like is it a psychological change? A physical change? Both?

Really my concern here is that it feels like it'd be a lot more interesting to look at what happens when there's this growing hive mind of radio hosts than tacking on a thing about them becoming monsters at the end; but perhaps there's a fun angle where some part of the hive mind growth causes it to happen and the story is almost…tragedy-like in style, y'know? It's like, us slowly watching a character we like turn from being cool and nice to a radio host to a rabid monster, y'know? As a like commentary on how e.g. stuff like fox news affects people say.

item.title: Re: Modern Day Soldier
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

My SCP idea is an entity that takes a form of a soldier (pretty much a U.S Soldier).

'pretty much' here implies it might not always be a U.S. Soldier? Or that it might be in some way different to a regular U.S. soldier beyond just the anomalous properties?

his form weakens by any sort of explosives

what does 'his form weakens' mean here? Like there's kinda an implication that this is a shapeshifting entity that just, appears as a soldier for whatever reason but it's not really clear why.

The soldier entity gets PTSD an effect that resembles PTSD, while in this state, he goes berserk, destroying everything he sees in a fit of rage.

I assume the start is an editing error?

This feels like an extremely shallow take on PTSD to the point of being offensive. It also feels like a weak attempt to justify including a 'rage state' in a SCP and I really do not recommend doing this.

Central Narrative:

This feels like a weird mishmash of 'how does the SCP behave' and 'what does the foundation think the SCP is' and…it feels directionless. Like it feels like it introduces a lot of concepts and uncertainty but it doesn't feel like it really does anything with it; there's no like overarching narrative, emotional or thematic arc so it feels a lot more like you're just kinda pointing at the SCP and saying 'wow isn't it interesting' than like, doing something to make a reader interested in it.

It might be handy to think of this section as being an opportunity to do a plot outline; where you show how you're telling the story and what the overall story is as well as the rough plot beats.

At the end of the day, this feels like it lacks the narrative cohesion required for it to work currently and it really feels like it just needs…focus and tightening up to be ready.

item.title: Re: Two Dimensional Love
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

Subject is inanimate but believed to be sentient.

Why do they think the scp is sentient?

Any male who enters the doll's line of "sight" has an approximate 3% chance of being imprinted on, upon which its effect manifests. Upon entering REM sleep, the victim has a 50% chance to enter a state similar to sleep paralysis, in which a vision of the doll will appear to them and gently caress them, leaving deep wounds.

This feels like it'd be pretty uncommon to occur and it feels like it raises questions like 'how did anyone discover this' and 'why does it only affect 3% of people'?

Any female (biological or transgender) the victim interacts with that is not of blood relation enters a similar state the next time they sleep in which they are executed in a manner similar to the Chinese Lingchi. This process is not painless.

This feels….weirdly cruel?

Article proceeds normally, with an addendum regarding its recovery from the belongings of a deceased Japanese man implied to be its creator after his "suicide" in police custody. Several experiment logs are listed near the end with the Foundation using D-Class to determine how it works.

So like…my concern here is that it feels like these experiment logs just won't really be interesting and they also feel like the kinda meat of this article? Like, the anomaly behaves in a way that's relatively straight forward and so I'm not sure what doing experiment logs adds to this beyond what's laid out in the description, y'know?

At the end of the day, this feels…kinda needlessly edgy but without any kind of pay off to it. It leaves an unpleasant taste in my mouth, though I can't quite put my finger on why; but it also feels like you don't really do much with the concept: like, this feels like the kinda thing that could be a huge inspection of how e.g. westerners appropriate japanese culture, or like, investigating the role gender plays here or something like that but instead we just have a generic doll that effectively fucks you to death and I'm really not that into that played straight, y'know?

item.title: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) Keep Him In The Dark
item.content:encoded:
In general, your core element's anomalies should make sense when considered altogether. Unconnected anomalous qualities can feel disconnected and confusing for a reader; a platypus that speaks French and poops iPhones is going to be considerably more difficult to fit in a story than, say, a surfer who can talk to dolphins.

How would that arc be represented in the rest of the article? A final interview can certainly help cement emotional growth, but we need to see how that growth began in the first place. cybersqyd puts it much better than I could below.

item.title: Re: SCP-something: Man unable to communicate properly
item.content:encoded:
It's not blasphemy to ask questions! We can think of a story as a way of building up tension and stakes for the reader. The ending, in that conventional line of thinking, should be a way of relieving that tension in a way that leaves the reader. This can be a resolution of a mystery, the end of an emotional arc, or even a twist that casts the previous elements in a drastically different light.

At the moment, it seems like you're trying to relieve the tension in a bunch of different ways at once without committing to any of them. Since each of your endings are 'twists' that are mostly unconnected to each other, it seems like the article "zig-zags" between different hints without taking the time to relate them to the actual narrative. Does that make sense?

item.title: Re: SCP Idea: "The Answer Sheet"
item.content:encoded:
Hey there cyliim, I’ll be critting your idea today!
Note that I am neither a particularly experienced nor an official reviewer, so take what I say with a grain of salt. With that being said, let’s begin the crit!

+ Open Section-by-Section +
– hide block

Elevator Pitch

So your pitch is a piece of paper possessed by an entity that has vast amounts of knowledge that can also control people. I… am not very keen on this idea. It’s pretty cliche and OP, as it knows all about the Foundation and the 05s, is hostile, and can control people. I’m getting Series I Keter vibes from this, which isn’t good. All in all, the concept seems very OP and cliche (also worth noting that the communication method is very reminiscent of Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets).

Central Narrative

It just… appeared in a storage closet in a secure Site? As a general rule, try to stay away from SCPs being discovered by appearing out of the blue in a convenient location. It can be seen as uncreative or lazy storytelling, and breaks readers’ suspension of disbelief. Other than that, there really isn’t very much substance behind the rest of the narrative. It gets tested upon, the 05s put on some strict safety measures, and that’s it. It just feels… boring.

Hook/Attention Grabber

The hook is unlikely to work, mostly because I am not curious how an eldritch, seemingly omniscient being knows about the Foundation. It’s simply a given.

+ Open General Thoughts +
I’m doubtful about this, buddy

The cliche, OP nature of your concept, the uninteresting narrative, and a boring hook make me quite doubtful about the potential of this concept as a whole, moreso of its reception on the mainsite if it were posted. As it stands, I’d probably downvote this is I found this as an article, and others probably would too.

I’d recommend three things:
1. Look at some of the more popular, recent articles (top rated of this month) for an idea of what people expect and enjoy from articles these days.
2. Check out the Guide Hub for a bunch of great essays to help aspiring writers for this Site such as yourself!
3. Contact some reviewers from the Butterfly Squad for some alternative opinions from experienced reviewers!

And finally, to sum up your your idea in one sentence1:
A sheet of paper possessed by a mysterious entity that knows almost everything about the Foundation, and can also control people who read its words.

And that’s it for my crit today. Thanks for reading, and I hope this helps!

Footnotes
1. This is to help you get an idea of the bare bones of what a critter sees when they read your summary. You may find something you don’t like or find that we’re getting the wrong impression.

item.title: The Blur *Seeking Greenlights*
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is as the name suggest, a blur or as also seen as a shadow. It inhabits the very south of Argentina, the being is observed to have human level or higher intelligence and exhibits some anomalous abilities.

Central Narrative: This SCP is on close watch by the foundation, it having no physical body and only appearing as a semi transparent blur or a shadow makes it impossible to contain. So the foundation has decided to watch it via satellite. While it is not hostile towards anything, it has been observed to kill plant based life around it, likely by an unconscious ability to soak moisture from its surroundings. The foundation has no clear hypothesis for its existence but the most widely accepted one is that the SCP is an alternate dimensional being that exist on a semi 4 dimensional level, allowing it to have no physical body, yet still visible to 3 dimensional beings, although this theory is not proven.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The SCP here has a lot of mystery around it, and I want to be able to not have a definitive answer what it exactly is. While the article will be mostly field notes by observers, I also want to explain why this SCP is as smart as a human and what ties it has to earth.

Additional Notes: I cant really explain everything here but if I can obtain 2 greenlights and make a sandbox, I can go into much better detail about this SCP and why it exist. Im not entirely sure where I can improve the central narrative to make it sound more interesting, but I have many ideas for this SCP so shoot your criticism at me so I can make this sound even more like a true SCP

item.content:encoded:

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional):

Page Layout (Optional): Regular SCP layout

Elevator Pitch: A regular looking piece of paper and an ink pen, that when written on using the aforementioned pen, grants a reply from the paper. The entity that replies through the paper is hyperintelligent, having knowledge of the O5 council and Level 5 clearance information that's withheld even from the researchers working on the SCP. It also has the ability to force anyone to grant any request that they read, which leads to many attempted escapes.

Central Narrative: A pair of entities, a pen and piece of paper, is discovered within an undisclosed SCP Site storage closet. After a junior researcher attempts to use the pen and paper together, he turns it in to his higher-ups, who begin experimentation on the entity. After discovering it's many abilities, such as it's incredible knowledge and it's way of making peopel complete requests, it is given strict safety and testing measures.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The way that the paper is very knowledagble about the Foundation, and how it can make people grant it's requests. It's a mysterious entity that much isn't known about, which leads to myriad tests on said entity.

Additional Notes: Looking especially for critique on how it makes people fufill the requests of readers, or if there's something that could work better with the idea.

Central Narrative: in the 1600s the Conquistadors found the tree (in theorized adolescent age) and documented it before leaving back for a colony only for them to be killed by a cult who was at the time worshipping another god. After they found the tree they began to worship it and built a supermassive cathedral around it, the tree and cathedral were later discovered by SCP in the 1960s by SCP who confiscated the whole thing and imprisoned the Cult. They later discovered that somehow the cult learned how to gain control over it. They even recovered SCP's, created SCP's or learned Anomylous abilities from the tree, these findings are contained in the Cathedral building itself.
